rationale: PCA scores highest because a single API call can produce a plausible, star-rated review in seconds, replacing what would take a human 10–30 minutes of authentic experience plus writing time — enabling mass deployment at near-zero marginal cost. RCG scores lowest because fake reviews are partially covered by existing FTC endorsement rules, EU consumer protection directives, and platform-level enforcement mechanisms that explicitly target inauthentic reviews, giving partial but real regulatory traction. DDI is high (4) because short-form, style-mimicking text is trivially paraphrased to evade classifiers, and no peer-reviewed detector achieves robust AUROC specifically on fake review identification under adversarial conditions.
